newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia workers agree to give up bonuses in rescue try.
newsitem.headline: Kia workers agree to give up bonuses in rescue try.

text.p: Union members of the troubled Kia Group announced on Monday they would give up their bonuses and monthly allowances to help normalise business in South Korea's eighth largest conglomerate, a group spokesman said.
A union statement read by the group spokesman said union members also agreed to give up holiday allowances which were expected to be paid in July. Union members did not mention their monthly wages.
Kia Group employees agreed to follow the union's decision.
Kia workers were scheduled to have bonus payments equal to 100 percent of their monthly salary four times a year, paid out in March, June, August and December.
"We will not have bonus payments from August until business improves," he said.
The statement said Kia Group needed an "emergency blood transfusion" for a rescue.
The union decided to lend 1.9 billion won from its reserves to management without condition and to conduct a 100 billion won fund-raising plan to help finance Kia Group subcontractors.
Union members also determined to give up five work-day summer holidays and to work over the weekend to meet the group's export commitments.
The spokesman said the 283 union leaders of Kia Group unions came up with the self-rescue plan.
Kia Group has also launched a campaign to sell one car per employee.
